description: The narrative layer of the Protocol Atlas: what each protocol is, who created it, what it carries, and which repository owns its specification. Product support for a protocol is not stated here; it comes from capability-snapshot.json, which is generated from the Core protocol registry.

protocols.name: Ordinals

origin.creator: Casey Rodarmor
origin.note: Ordinal theory numbers individual satoshis and lets arbitrary content be inscribed onto them.

protocols.purpose: Assigns a stable ordinal number to every satoshi and attaches content to individual satoshis, producing digital artifacts that move as ordinary UTXOs.
protocols.universeImplementation: bitcoinuniverseio/index-ordinals and a Universe-operated ord server

protocols.name: BRC-20
protocols.carrier: Ordinals inscription carrying a JSON payload

origin.creator: domo
origin.note: An experiment in fungible tokens expressed entirely as inscribed JSON, indexed off-chain.

protocols.purpose: Fungible tokens defined by inscribed JSON operations, where balances are computed by indexers rather than enforced by consensus.

protocols.name: Runes

origin.creator: Casey Rodarmor
origin.note: Activated at block 840,000. Designed to be UTXO-native and to avoid the junk-UTXO problem of inscription-based tokens.

protocols.purpose: UTXO-native fungible tokens whose balances live in transaction outputs and move by ordinary spending, with etching, minting, and edicts encoded in a single OP_RETURN.
protocols.universeImplementation: bitcoinuniverseio/index-runes and a Universe-operated ord rune index

protocols.name: Runes (Native)

origin.note: Not a separate protocol. A Universe read path that serves Rune balances directly from Universe infrastructure.

protocols.purpose: The first-party read path for Runes state, separated in the product so that Rune data served from Universe infrastructure is distinguishable from any other source.

protocols.name: Bitcoin Stamps
protocols.carrier: Bare multisig and OP_RETURN outputs carrying encoded data

origin.creator: Mike In Space
origin.note: Stores image data in transaction outputs that cannot be pruned, aiming for permanence stronger than witness data.

protocols.purpose: Immutable on-chain images stored in unprunable transaction outputs, indexed through the Counterparty data layer.

protocols.name: SRC-20
protocols.carrier: Stamps data outputs carrying a JSON payload

origin.creator: The Bitcoin Stamps community
origin.note: A fungible-token layer built on the Stamps data-carrier model rather than on inscriptions.

protocols.purpose: Fungible tokens whose operations are stored in unprunable Stamps outputs and whose balances are computed by Stamps indexers.

protocols.name: SRC-101
protocols.carrier: Stamps data outputs carrying a JSON payload

origin.creator: The Bitcoin Stamps community
origin.note: Adds a naming layer to the Stamps data model.

protocols.purpose: On-chain names recorded through the Stamps data carrier, with ownership tracked by Stamps indexers.

protocols.name: Atomicals

origin.creator: Arthur (atomicals.xyz)
origin.note: A general digital-object protocol using commit and reveal transactions.

protocols.purpose: Digital objects minted through commit and reveal, covering non-fungible items, realms, containers, and the data model that ARC-20 builds on.

protocols.name: ARC-20

origin.creator: Arthur (atomicals.xyz)
origin.note: Tokens are satoshis. One token is one satoshi, so token supply is real bitcoin.

protocols.purpose: Fungible tokens where one token is exactly one satoshi, so balances move as coloured sats and splitting follows output ordering rules.

protocols.name: Atomicals NFTs
protocols.purpose: Non-fungible Atomicals digital objects, including collection items minted through decentralised mint rules.

protocols.name: Realms
protocols.purpose: Top-level names in the Atomicals naming system, claimed by satisfying the protocol's mint rules.

protocols.name: Subrealms
protocols.purpose: Names minted underneath a Realm, subject to the rules the parent Realm publishes.

protocols.name: AVM
protocols.purpose: The Atomicals virtual machine, an execution model layered on the Atomicals data format.

protocols.name: Alkanes
protocols.carrier: Protostone inside an OP_RETURN runestone envelope

origin.creator: The Alkanes project
origin.note: Smart contracts compiled to WebAssembly, with balances carried as protorunes.

protocols.purpose: A metaprotocol placing WebAssembly contract execution over Bitcoin, where token balances travel as protorunes in protostones.

protocols.name: Mezcal
protocols.purpose: A fungible-token protocol whose transfer instructions are written as a compact JSON payload in an OP_RETURN output.

protocols.name: TAP
protocols.carrier: Ordinals inscription carrying a TAP envelope

origin.creator: The Trac ecosystem
origin.note: Extends the inscribed-token idea with authority-based operations and privileged mints.

protocols.purpose: An inscribed token protocol with a wider operation set than BRC-20, including token authority and privileged operations.

protocols.name: TAP on Doge
protocols.carrier: Doginals inscription carrying a TAP envelope
protocols.purpose: The TAP protocol as applied to Dogecoin inscriptions.

protocols.name: DMT
protocols.carrier: Ordinals inscription referencing a deployed element
protocols.purpose: Digital Matter Theory: tokens whose content is derived deterministically from block data rather than stored in each mint.
protocols.specificationHome: Maintained upstream by the Trac ecosystem

protocols.name: Bitmap
protocols.purpose: Claims of Bitcoin blocks as addressable districts, established by the first valid inscription for a block number.
protocols.specificationHome: Maintained upstream by the Bitmap community

protocols.name: UNAT
protocols.purpose: Natural-asset digital artifacts recorded through inscriptions and rendered from deterministic rules.

protocols.name: Bitcoin Names
protocols.purpose: Names claimed by inscription, resolved by first-valid-claim indexing rules.

protocols.name: BLOCK-20
protocols.purpose: A token protocol whose mint validity is tied to block-derived proof rather than open minting.

protocols.name: DUST-20
protocols.carrier: Inscription for deploy and mint, then an ordinary spend for movement
protocols.purpose: Tokens whose units are carried by the satoshis holding them. A deploy inscription fixes how many satoshis back one unit, a mint inscription must sit in an output holding exactly that many, and movement is an ordinary spend whose output layout decides which whole units survive.

protocols.name: OP-20
protocols.purpose: A token protocol using plain OP_RETURN data outputs as its only carrier.

protocols.name: OP Names
protocols.purpose: Names registered through OP_RETURN data outputs.
protocols.universeImplementation: bitcoinuniverseio/index-op20 (the OP Names authority is colocated there, not in index-names)

protocols.name: OP Inscriptions
protocols.purpose: Content records written directly into OP_RETURN outputs rather than witness data.

protocols.name: OP_DROP
protocols.carrier: Script witness data consumed by OP_DROP

origin.creator: Bitcoin Universe
origin.note: An original Bitcoin Universe carrier design.

protocols.purpose: A data carrier that places payloads in script witness data removed from the stack by OP_DROP, giving a carrier distinct from both inscriptions and OP_RETURN.

protocols.name: Drops

origin.creator: Bitcoin Universe
origin.note: The application protocol built on the OP_DROP carrier.

protocols.purpose: Media-first artifacts and agreements recorded through the OP_DROP carrier, including Drop Pacts.

protocols.name: Doginals
protocols.purpose: Ordinals-style inscriptions applied to Dogecoin.

protocols.name: DRC-20
protocols.carrier: Doginals inscription carrying a JSON payload
protocols.purpose: The BRC-20 token model applied to Dogecoin inscriptions.

protocols.name: Dunes

origin.creator: The Dogecoin dunes community
origin.note: The Runes design applied to Dogecoin. A dunestone carries the same shape as a runestone: edicts, an optional etching, an optional pointer, and a cenotaph flag for a malformed message.

protocols.purpose: UTXO-native fungible tokens on Dogecoin, encoded as a dunestone in an OP_RETURN output. Balances live in transaction outputs and move by ordinary spending, with etching, minting, and edicts in a single data output.

protocols.name: CAT-20
protocols.purpose: Fungible tokens enforced by covenant constructions rather than by indexer convention.

protocols.name: CAT-721
protocols.purpose: The non-fungible counterpart to CAT-20, using the same covenant model.

protocols.name: Rare Sats
protocols.purpose: Satoshis distinguished by ordinal-theory rarity, such as block firsts and cycle boundaries, tracked as collectible outputs.

protocols.name: Ordex

origin.creator: Bitcoin Universe
origin.note: A routing and evidence layer over openly published PSBT orders.

protocols.purpose: An order and evidence format for exchanging Ordinals using signed PSBTs, with verification against a local node rather than a trusted marketplace.

protocols.name: ChainBloom
protocols.purpose: Generative on-chain artwork whose output is derived deterministically from chain data, so every viewer renders the same result.

protocols.name: Zerdinals

origin.creator: Bitcoin Universe
origin.note: Digital artifacts native to Zcash, with transparent and shielded considerations.

protocols.purpose: Digital artifacts recorded on Zcash, with explicit handling of the difference between transparent and shielded activity.

protocols.name: Z-Runes
protocols.purpose: Fungible tokens native to Zcash, including the ZRC-20 token standard.

protocols.name: Witness Circles
protocols.purpose: Membership records established by mutual witnessing, where a circle's state is derived from the commitments its members publish.

protocols.name: Tandem
protocols.carrier: An exact 20,000 satoshi native SegWit 2-of-2 P2WSH output
protocols.purpose: An object two people create and hold together. The active object is an exact 2-of-2 output, so both current keys are required for any cooperative action: adding a chapter, rotating one or both keys, or closing. If collaboration stops, a recovery transaction prepared in advance becomes usable once its relative lock matures.

protocols.name: Patina
protocols.purpose: A provenance layer that accumulates verifiable history over an existing artifact rather than creating a new asset.

protocols.name: Bitcoin
protocols.purpose: The base chain itself: plain value held in unspent transaction outputs, which every protocol above ultimately rides on.
protocols.specificationHome: Bitcoin Core and the BIP process, maintained upstream
